transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-22
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Tomas Ivanov (Redwood SE), John Patel (Sparrow Head of ML), Leah Ortiz (Platform), Ethan Wu (Security), Priya Singh (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
Customer is scoping a 4-6 week POC to decide between hosted, dedicated or private deployment. Success criteria include latency SLOs, cost per inference, and data residency/compliance. Need a benchmark plan, representative load, and security checklist. Next steps agreed: send sizing/pricing, bench plan, and schedule kickoff.

Topics discussed: POC goals; Traffic profile and sizing; Benchmark plan (throughput/latency/cost); Security & compliance constraints; Decision criteria and timeline; Pilot rollout steps.

Action items (parsed in call): see metadata list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maria (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'll kick us off. Quick intros?
[00:12] John (Sparrow): Hi, John Patel here, head of ML at Sparrow — we own the triage assistant project.
[00:17] Leah (Sparrow): Leah, platform eng, I'll own infra and integration.
[00:20] Ethan (Sparrow): Ethan, security.
[00:22] Priya (Sparrow): Priya, product.
[00:25] Maria: Great. Tomas from our side is the SE, he'll run through performance and the benchmark plan.
[00:30] Tomas (Redwood SE): Thanks. The objective today is to scope a POC that helps you pick between Redwood hosted, Dedicated capacity, or Private (VPC/air-gapped) deployment. We'll cover success criteria, workload sizing, what we'll measure in benchmarks, and a proposed timeline.
[00:45] John: Perfect. High level: our triage assistant gets user messages, we do a multi-step pipeline — initial classification, then short generation for the summary, and an embeddings + rerank stage. We're most worried about latency for the generation step and cost for the embeddings since that's a heavy part.
[01:10] Tomas: Okay, can you give us rough rps and token counts so we can size?
[01:15] John: Sure. Peak is about 250 rps aggregate across services during business hours, but the triage assistant itself is closer to 40 to 60 rps. Average completion is 45 tokens; in the worst case 200 tokens. Embeddings calls are batched in the current pipeline — roughly 10K embed calls per hour during peak windows.
[01:40] Leah: Also important: we have strict PHI handling for certain fields so data residency and KMS integration are must-haves.
[01:48] Ethan: Correct. We need SOC-2 controls, audit logs, and the ability to use our KMS/HSM. Private deployment is attractive for that reason, but cost and operational burden are concerns.
[02:05] Maria: Thanks — that helps. Tomas, what are the levers here?
[02:09] Tomas: For POC scoping, we look at 3 axis: latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99), throughput (RPS/concurrency), and cost (per token / per embed). The deployment mode affects each axis: Hosted is fastest to set up and easiest to scale but less control over KMS; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and reserved GPU pools; Private gives full control for KMS and network but needs infra ops.
[02:40] Priya: On latency, what should we target for p95 given our numbers? John listed ~45 tokens avg — we need it snappy in UI.
[02:47] Tomas: For short generations ~32-64 tokens, a reasonable target p95 would be ~400-700ms depending on model family. If you need sub-200ms p95 we usually look at specialized batching, smaller quantized models or colocated serving which pushes towards Dedicated or Private.
[03:05] John: Interesting. Our product team wants p95 < 500ms for the summary step to keep UI latency acceptable.
[03:12] Tomas: That's achievable on Dedicated with proper batching and KV caching, and sometimes on Hosted if the traffic shape is steady and model choice is optimized. We'll put numbers in the bench plan.
[03:24] Leah: For the embeddings — cost per embed matters. Do you have typical cost deltas between hosted and dedicated?
[03:30] Maria: High level, hosted is pay-as-you-go; unit cost is visible in the console. Dedicated lowers cost per token by ~25-50% depending on utilization and quantization. Private can be cheaper at high scale but ops overhead and upfront commitments push the break-even point out. We'll show scenarios.
[03:53] Ethan: Security question — can hosted integrate with our KMS for customer-managed keys?
[03:58] Maria: Hosted supports envelope encryption with our KMS integrations for some tiers; for full key custody and HSM-backed keys you typically look at Private. There are also Dedicated options with customer-owned keys depending on contract. We'll need to confirm the exact KMS flow for your account.
[04:15] Tomas: For the bench plan, we propose three phases: 1) smoke test on hosted with a small traffic replay to validate correctness and baseline latency; 2) formal throughput and p95 measurements using your representative traffic (we ask for a 7-day sample logs); 3) Dedicated pilot (if needed) to compare cost and p99 at scale. Each phase has scripted steps and metrics capture.
[04:40] John: How long for each phase? We're aiming to decide in 4-6 weeks total.
[04:45] Tomas: Roughly: phase 1 = 3 days, phase 2 = 1 week of runs and analysis, phase 3 = 2-3 weeks to provision Dedicated and run scaled tests. So 4 weeks is tight but possible if we run in parallel and you provide logs quickly.
[05:05] Priya: What about fallback behavior and graceful degradation? Say Dedicated runs out of capacity.
[05:10] Maria: You can set routing policies to fallback to hosted model variants or smaller models; Redwood has built-in fallbacks. We'll walk through the routing policy config in the console during the pilot.
[05:24] Leah: A couple infra notes: our infra team is primarily Kubernetes on EKS. If we do Private we need an operator guide.
[05:31] Tomas: We have an on-prem package and VPC deployment docs. For Private deployment we'll need network egress rules, subnets for GPUs, and an onboarding window to install the control plane. That usually adds 1-2 weeks to setup.
[05:50] Ethan: Audit logs: how long are logs retained? We need 1 year for compliance.
[05:55] Maria: Console retention is configurable; long-term retention is an add-on. For Private deployments you can ship logs to your ELK/Splunk with full retention. We'll get exact retention SLA in the security doc.
[06:10] John: Back to benchmarks: what's the standard measurement for embedding cost — do you measure per-embedding unit or per token?
[06:18] Tomas: Embeddings are measured per request (per vector), price per 1K vectors is common. We'll report unit cost per vector and projected monthly cost using your peak numbers. We'll include batching impact (e.g., batching 32 vectors reduces GPU overhead).
[06:35] Leah: Our traffic shape is bursty: 30-40 rps steady, spikes to 250 for scheduled processing windows. How does autoscaling behave?
[06:43] Tomas: Hosted autoscale is transparent; Dedicated has autoscale policies with burst capacity options. For Private you'd configure autoscaling with your infra (we provide recommendations). The key is to stress the burst profile in the benchmarks.
[07:00] Maria: Can you describe your success criteria beyond latency — what will make POC a "success" from product/ops/security lenses?
[07:09] Priya: Product: p95 < 500ms for summary, error rate <0.2% during peak.
[07:14] John: ML: model fidelity within 5% of our baseline on eval prompt set (we have an eval suite).
[07:20] Leah: Ops: integration with SSO and ability to route through VPC peering; also clear rollback path.
[07:25] Ethan: Security: KMS-compatibility, SOC2 controls, and audit logs to our SIEM.
[07:31] Tomas: Good. We'll bake those into the acceptance criteria in the bench report.
[07:36] John: About models — are we limited to certain families on Dedicated vs Hosted? We want some of the newer open models with quantization.
[07:44] Tomas: We support a curated set across both Hosted and Dedicated. Dedicated gives you more flexibility for custom model variants and quantization profiles. Private is the most flexible if you need binary-level control. We'll list compatible model families in the proposal.
[07:58] Maria: Competitors question — I know you mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI internally. What would push you away from a hosted vendor?
[08:05] John: It's mostly about cost and control. If we can't get KMS or audit log parity, that's a blocker. Also predictable latency under burst — we've seen noisy neighbors on public endpoints elsewhere.
[08:17] Tomas: Understood. We'll include test cases to check for noisy neighbor effects — e.g., run background load in Dedicated and measure p99 variance.
[08:28] Leah: On timeline, we want a pilot in prod-like environment with canary traffic. Are you able to do that on Hosted?
[08:35] Maria: Yes, you can run canary routes against Hosted. For Dedicated we can put dedicated pool behind your canary and manage rollout. For Private you'd manage the canary rollout in your infra but we provide rollout guides.
[08:50] Priya: One nuance — we need per-route cost attribution to product teams.
[08:55] Tomas: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and per-route breakdowns; we'll show a sample in the billing demo.
[09:03] John: Ok, what bench metrics will you capture exactly?
[09:07] Tomas: We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput (rps), cost per request, GPU utilization, batching efficiency (tokens per second per GPU), and regression on your eval prompts (quality). We'll also capture cold start behavior and KV cache hit rate.
[09:25] Priya: Cold start is critical for our async workers.
[09:28] Tomas: We'll add a cold-start test with modeled restarts.
[09:32] Maria: Anything else on security?
[09:35] Ethan: Two items: SAML SSO with okta; ability to disable logs for sensitive fields before sending.
[09:42] Tomas: Ok, for logging we have redaction rules and on Private you can avoid sending logs to our cloud. The SAML flow is supported for enterprise tiers. We'll include step-by-step steps in the security checklist.
[09:55] Maria: I'm going to summarize the plan and timeline: Sparrow provides logs and eval suite by 2025-05-24; Maria sends pricing and Dedicated sizing by 2025-05-26; Tomas sends bench plan by 2025-05-28; kickoff pilot week of 2025-05-29. Pilot runs 2-3 weeks with concurrent Hosted smoke and Dedicated tests depending on your preference. Decision checkpoint targeted 2025-06-19. Does that align?
[10:22] John: Yes, that works.
[10:24] Leah: Works for infra.
[10:25] Ethan: Works.
[10:27] Tomas: One more technical note — for embeddings batching you might get 2-3x GPU efficiency if you move batching to client side vs server-side; we'll show tradeoffs.
[10:38] Priya: What's the roll-out risk? If performance regresses after we switch traffic, what's the fallback?
[10:42] Maria: Rollbacks are straightforward with route-based configs; you can A/B or canary and automatically fallback to previous model variant or hosted pool if error thresholds exceed. We'll document the steps.
[10:55] John: Good. Any blockers for the POC start?
[10:58] Leah: We need an IP allowlist or peering details for Dedicated and Private.
[11:02] Maria: We'll open a ticket to coordinate network details.
[11:05] Ethan: And legal will need DPA clarifications.
[11:09] Maria: I'll loop in legal and send the DPA template.
[11:13] Tomas: For the bench scripts we'll use a replay harness and a small eval runner that measures quality per prompt set and emits metrics to a Grafana dashboard. We'll share the harness repo link.
[11:26] John: Can you also include cost sensitivity analysis? Like break-even points for Dedicated vs Private at monthly RPS?
[11:31] Maria: Yes, we'll provide a cost model with utilization assumptions.
[11:34] Tomas: Minor note: if you want sub-200ms p95 you're effectively looking at colocated GPUs with smaller models or strong quantization; we'll include a matrix.
[11:45] Priya: Ok. Anything else?
[11:48] Maria: Quick recap of next steps (I'll say them and we'll capture in the notes): Maria send pricing/sizing; Tomas send benchmark plan and harness; Sparrow send logs and eval suite; schedule kickoff.
[12:03] John: Thanks, everyone.
[12:06] Leah: Thanks.
[12:08] Ethan: Bye.
